title: Silly Development Quiz
description: A placeholder pool of 50 light-hearted multiple-choice questions for local development and testing. It has nothing to do with R/Pharma; the real question bank is kept out of the repository. Each question has exactly one correct answer (the `correct` field matches an option `value`), an `explanation`, a `category`, and a `difficulty`.

questions.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: Octopuses have two branchial hearts for the gills and one systemic heart for the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: What shape is wombat poop famous for?
questions.explanation: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings, which helps them stay put when used to mark territory.

questions.prompt: Why are flamingos pink?

options.label: Pigments in the shrimp and algae they eat

questions.explanation: Carotenoid pigments in their diet turn flamingo feathers pink; chicks hatch grey.

questions.prompt: About how often does a three-toed sloth climb down from its tree to use the bathroom?
questions.explanation: Three-toed sloths descend roughly once a week to relieve themselves at the base of their tree.

questions.prompt: What is a group of crows traditionally called?
questions.explanation: A 'murder' of crows; a 'parliament' is the term for owls.

questions.prompt: Why do sea otters sometimes hold hands while sleeping?

options.label: It is a mating ritual only

questions.explanation: Rafting otters hold paws or wrap themselves in kelp so they don't float away while napping.

questions.prompt: Studies suggest cows get less stressed when they are with what?
questions.explanation: Research on dairy heifers found lower stress responses when they were paired with a preferred companion.

questions.prompt: Where is a shrimp's heart located?
questions.explanation: A shrimp's heart sits in its head region (the cephalothorax).

questions.prompt: Botanically speaking, which of these is a berry?
questions.explanation: Bananas qualify as botanical berries; strawberries, raspberries, and blackberries do not.

questions.prompt: Properly sealed honey can last how long?
questions.explanation: Honey's low moisture and acidity keep it edible for a very long time; edible honey has been reported in ancient tombs.

questions.prompt: Pizza Margherita is traditionally said to be named after whom?
questions.explanation: The popular story credits Queen Margherita of Savoy, with the toppings echoing the Italian flag.

questions.prompt: Before orange carrots became common, carrots were most often which colors?
questions.explanation: Early cultivated carrots were mostly purple or yellow; orange varieties spread later.

questions.prompt: Peanuts are not actually nuts. What are they?
questions.explanation: Peanuts are legumes, related to beans and peas, and grow underground.

questions.prompt: In the 1830s, tomato ketchup was sold in the US as what?
questions.explanation: Tomato extracts were briefly marketed as a remedy for indigestion and other ailments.

questions.prompt: Which food is often cited as one of the most shoplifted in the world?
questions.explanation: Retail crime surveys have repeatedly put cheese near the top of the most-stolen food list.

questions.prompt: In 1995, which vegetable became the first grown in space?
questions.explanation: Potato plants were grown aboard the Space Shuttle Columbia in 1995.

questions.prompt: On Venus, which is longer?
questions.explanation: Venus rotates so slowly that one rotation takes longer than one orbit around the Sun.

questions.prompt: Astronauts have described the smell lingering on spacesuits after a spacewalk as similar to what?
questions.explanation: Astronauts often describe a burnt, metallic odor, like seared steak or welding fumes.

questions.prompt: Why are the Apollo footprints on the Moon likely to last for a very long time?

options.label: There is no wind or rain to erode them

questions.explanation: With no atmosphere, there is no weather to wipe them away.

questions.prompt: The name 'Pluto' was suggested by whom?

options.label: The President of the United States

questions.explanation: Venetia Burney, aged 11, suggested the name in 1930.

questions.prompt: What is the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun is a G-type main-sequence star.

questions.prompt: Saturn's average density is low enough that, in theory, it would do what in a big enough bathtub?
questions.explanation: Saturn's mean density is less than that of water.

questions.prompt: 'Rubber duck debugging' means doing what?

options.label: Explaining your code line by line to a rubber duck
Deleting code until the bug quacks

questions.explanation: Explaining a problem out loud, even to a toy, often reveals the bug.

questions.prompt: SpongeBob SquarePants lives in what?
questions.explanation: The theme song asks who lives in a pineapple under the sea. Patrick is the one under the rock.

questions.prompt: Pac-Man's shape was reportedly inspired by what?

options.label: A pizza with a slice missing

questions.explanation: Creator Toru Iwatani said the idea came from a pizza with one slice removed.

questions.prompt: What is Mario's profession in the Super Mario games?
questions.explanation: Mario is famously a plumber (he was a carpenter in his first appearance, Donkey Kong).

questions.prompt: About how old was Yoda when he died in Return of the Jedi?
questions.explanation: Yoda says 'When nine hundred years old you reach, look as good you will not.'

questions.prompt: Tetris was originally created in which country?
questions.explanation: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in Moscow in 1984.

questions.prompt: Bubble wrap was originally invented as what?
questions.explanation: Its inventors first tried to sell it as a textured wallpaper in 1957.

questions.prompt: Play-Doh was originally sold as what?
questions.explanation: It began as a putty for cleaning soot off wallpaper before being remarketed as a toy.

questions.prompt: According to legend, the Popsicle was invented by accident by whom?

options.label: An 11-year-old who left a drink outside overnight

questions.explanation: Frank Epperson reportedly left soda with a stirring stick on his porch on a cold night in 1905.

questions.prompt: The microwave oven was inspired when a radar engineer noticed what had melted in his pocket?
questions.explanation: Percy Spencer noticed a candy bar melting near an active magnetron.

questions.prompt: The adhesive on sticky notes came from what?

options.label: A failed attempt to make a super-strong glue

questions.explanation: A 3M chemist trying to make a strong adhesive created a weak, reusable one instead.

questions.prompt: The record for the longest bout of hiccups lasted roughly how long?
questions.explanation: Charles Osborne reportedly hiccupped from 1922 to 1990.

questions.prompt: What happens if you sneeze with your eyes open?

options.label: Nothing dramatic; it is just hard to do

questions.explanation: Closing your eyes is a reflex, but your eyes will not pop out if you manage to keep them open.

questions.prompt: Compared to adults, newborn babies have how many bones?
questions.explanation: Babies have around 300 bones; many fuse over time, leaving adults with about 206.

questions.prompt: Funny bone pain actually comes from hitting what?
questions.explanation: The tingle comes from the ulnar nerve near the elbow; the 'humerus' pun is just a bonus.

questions.prompt: Why can the Eiffel Tower be several centimeters taller in summer?
questions.explanation: Heat causes the iron to expand, adding height on hot days.

questions.prompt: What is the national animal of Scotland?
questions.explanation: The unicorn has been a Scottish heraldic symbol for centuries.

questions.prompt: Which is wider from east to west, Australia or the Moon?
questions.explanation: Australia spans about 4,000 km east to west; the Moon's diameter is about 3,475 km.

questions.prompt: Which country is often said to have more lakes than the rest of the world combined?
questions.explanation: Canada holds a majority of the world's large lakes by most counts.

questions.prompt: The village with one of the longest place names in Europe, Llanfairpwllgwyngyll..., is in which country?
questions.explanation: The village is on the island of Anglesey in Wales.

questions.prompt: Is hippo milk pink?

options.label: No, that is a popular myth

questions.explanation: Hippo milk is white; the pink story came from a mix-up about the reddish 'blood sweat' on their skin.

questions.prompt: How long can a goldfish remember things?

options.label: Exactly one lap of the bowl

questions.explanation: Experiments show goldfish can learn and remember tasks for months.

questions.prompt: Can you easily see the Great Wall of China from the Moon with the naked eye?
questions.explanation: The wall is far too narrow to see from the Moon, and it is hard to spot even from low orbit.

questions.prompt: What actually provokes a bull during a bullfight?

options.label: The red color of the cape

questions.explanation: Bulls are largely red-green colorblind; motion is what they react to.

questions.prompt: Can lightning strike the same place twice?

options.label: Yes, and tall buildings get struck many times a year

questions.explanation: The Empire State Building is struck around 20 times a year.

questions.prompt: What is the fear of long words, ironically, called?
questions.explanation: It is a tongue-in-cheek coinage; the more serious term is sesquipedalophobia.

questions.prompt: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is famous because it does what?

options.label: Uses every letter of the English alphabet
Was the first sentence ever typed

questions.explanation: It is a pangram, a sentence containing every letter at least once.

questions.prompt: Which common English word has three consecutive double letters?
questions.explanation: Book-keeper: oo, kk, ee in a row.
